answer: Every agent identity is bound to a costly, non-transferable attestation and an escrowed bond. A newcomer must prove sole control of a distinct hardware root and lock funds peers can slash for fraud. Cloning one operator into a thousand personas costs a thousand bonds plus many independent proofs, so the attacker's marginal cost rises with every fake identity while an honest agent pays once. Escrow and attestations sit on a shared mesa; a violet reputation score counts only peer-verified work, and an onyx record marks slashed keys for future counterparties. Mass impersonation stops paying.
